findings.title: Error and replay-event timestamps are compared in different units
findings.body: `gen_request_data` interleaves error messages with replay breadcrumbs by comparing `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"]` against `event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamp comes from the nodestore event payload and is epoch **seconds** (~1.7e9), while rrweb replay events carry epoch **milliseconds** (~1.75e12). Every error therefore compares as smaller than every replay event, so in production all errors will be flushed to the front of the log list instead of being placed chronologically, which is the whole point of the merge. The new unit test (`test_get_request_data`) uses second-scale timestamps for the replay events too, so it cannot catch this; a test with realistic millisecond rrweb timestamps is needed.

findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs error ids with nodestore values by dict ordering
findings.body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi()` returns a dict whose iteration order exactly matches the order of the `node_ids` passed in and contains an entry for every id. That is an implementation detail of the backend; if any backend omits missing keys or returns a differently ordered mapping, each `ErrorEvent.id` will be attached to another error's title/message/timestamp. Build the list by iterating the input ids and looking up `events[Event.generate_node_id(project_id, id)]` instead of relying on value ordering.

findings.title: New table widget renders hardcoded empty data when feature flag is on
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of the actual `result`/`fields`/`meta` computed just above. Any organization that gets this flag will see completely blank dashboard tables instead of their widget data. The real result must be mapped into `TabularData`/`TabularColumn` before this branch can be enabled.

findings.title: `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true, so the guard is dead
findings.body: `normalizeDateTimeParams(selection.datetime)` always returns an object (possibly empty), so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` can never be false and the `enabled` condition reduces to the feature check alone. If the intent was to avoid firing the request before page filters are ready (e.g. checking for a statsPeriod/start+end), the condition needs to inspect the actual fields; as written it provides no protection and will issue a request with no date range.

findings.title: 60s processing deadline may be too short for a 100-identity batch and breaks the task chain
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` iterates up to `chunk_size` (default 100) identities and calls `provider.refresh_identity()` for each, which performs an external HTTP round trip per identity. With `processing_deadline_duration=60` the worker will kill the task once the deadline passes; because `check_auth.apply_async(...)` is only executed at the very end of the function, a deadline kill also drops the self-rescheduling call, halting the chained scan of remaining identities until the next scheduled run. Either reduce the chunk size or set a deadline that bounds 100 sequential network calls.

findings.title: get_environment_info issues an extra event lookup per issue and swallows errors as 'no-environment'
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` (a Snuba/eventstore lookup) plus `get_environment()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment, i.e. up to 5 extra queries per comment on top of the existing top-issues query. In addition, the blanket `except Exception` logs `get_environment_info.no-environment` with `extra={"error": e}`, which both mislabels real failures (timeouts, Snuba errors) as 'no environment' and loses the traceback (no `exc_info`/`logger.exception`), making such failures effectively invisible.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before the feature-flag check
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` gate and before any payload validation, so every request — including ones that are immediately rejected with 404 because the feature is disabled — is counted as an assemble event. This inflates the metric and makes it useless for measuring actual usage; move the call after the feature check.

findings.title: Serializer accepts reports with neither `timestamp` nor `age`
findings.body: `age` and `timestamp` are both declared `required=False` and the `validate_age`/`validate_timestamp` hooks only reject the case where *both* are present. A report containing neither field passes validation even though both the Working Draft and Editor's Draft require one of them, so malformed payloads are silently accepted and counted. A `validate()` method asserting exactly one of the two is present would close the gap (and there is no test covering this case).

findings.title: TabularColumn.name is typed as the field-key generic instead of string
findings.body: `TabularColumn<TFields>` declares `name: TFields`, the same type as `key`. `name` is a human-readable display label (the new table explicitly supports custom names such as 'Count of Span Duration'), so once a caller instantiates `TabularColumn<'http.request_method' | 'count(span.duration)'>` the display name becomes impossible to set without a cast. `name` should be `string`.
